records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:24 — discourse_expires_in 1.minute is applied unconditionally, so the transient 'loading' response (which self-reloads via JS) can be cached for a minute even though the topic may already be available on next request
records.rationale: In EmbedController#best, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is called after the conditional that may `render 'loading'` (when `topic_id` is nil). The loading view includes JS that reloads after 30s, but with a 1-minute cache TTL the browser/proxy could cache and re-serve the loading response on reload, delaying display of the now-available topic.

records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:33 — TopicRetriever (a lib class) directly instantiates and executes Jobs::PollFeed, coupling a plain retrieval library to the job-queue layer instead of enqueuing or injecting the dependency
records.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#perform_retrieve, the plain library class TopicRetriever directly creates and runs a scheduled job class: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`. This concretely couples retrieval logic to the jobs layer (and runs the job inline rather than enqueueing/injecting), which is a substantive architecture/maintenance concern grounded in the diff, not a functional defect by itself.

records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — Access control relies on comparing request.referer host to embeddable_host, but Referer is a client-supplied header that non-browser clients can freely spoof, making this an unreliable security boundary
records.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is granted/denied based on `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and then it sets `X-Frame-Options = ALLOWALL`. Because `Referer` is a client-supplied header, non-browser clients (or proxies) can spoof it, bypassing this check and accessing the embed endpoint; this security decision is directly shown in the diff.
